sentences.zh: 顯德二年春正月辛未朔，帝不受朝賀。

translations.literal: In spring of the second year of Xiande, on the first day of the first month (day xinwei, new moon), the Emperor did not accept court congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinwei new moon of the first month of spring in Xiande 2, the Emperor declined the usual court congratulations.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，詔：「在朝文班，各舉堪為令錄者一人，雖姻族近親，亦無妨嫌。

translations.literal: On day xinmao, an edict: "Among the civil officials at court, each shall recommend one person fit to serve as county magistrate or recorder; even close relatives by marriage need not be excluded."
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao an edict stated: “Each civil official at court shall nominate one person qualified for county magistrate or recorder—even a close kinsman by marriage is not barred.”

sentences.zh: 授官之日，各署舉主姓名，若在官貪濁不任、懦弱不理，並量事狀重輕，連坐舉主。

translations.literal: On the day of appointment, each shall record the recommender's name; if the appointee while in office is corrupt and unfit, or timid and unable to govern, the severity of the case shall be weighed, and the recommender shall be punished by association.
translations.idiomatic: At appointment each nominee’s recommender shall be named on record; if the appointee proves corrupt, incompetent, timid, or neglectful in office, the recommender shall share liability according to the gravity of the offense.

sentences.zh: 」乙未，詔：「應逃戶莊田，並許人請射承佃，供納稅租：如三周年內本戶來歸者，其莊田不計荒熟，並交還一半；

translations.literal: " On day yiwei, an edict: "As to estate fields of absconding households, all are permitted to be bid for and leased by others, who shall pay taxes and rent: if the original household returns within three years, its estate fields, whether waste or cultivated, shall be returned in half;
translations.idiomatic: ” On yiwei an edict declared: “Estate fields left by absconding households may be bid for and leased by others, who shall pay tax and rent; if the original household returns within three years, half the fields—whether fallow or cultivated—shall be restored to them;

sentences.zh: 五周年內歸業者，三分交還一分；

translations.literal: if they return to their occupation within five years, one part in three shall be returned;
translations.idiomatic: if they resume farming within five years, one-third shall be returned;

sentences.zh: 如五周年外歸業者，其莊田除本戶墳塋外，不在交付之限。

translations.literal: if they return to their occupation after five years, their estate fields, except for the original household's graves, are not within the limit of delivery.
translations.idiomatic: if they return after five years, the fields need not be returned except for the family burial grounds.

sentences.zh: 其近北地諸州，應有陷蕃人戶，自蕃界來歸業者：五周年內來者，三分交還二分；

translations.literal: In the northern border prefectures, as to households that fell into the barbarians' hands and return from the barbarian frontier to resume their occupation: those who come within five years shall have two parts in three returned;
translations.idiomatic: In northern border prefectures, households lost to the Khitan who return from beyond the frontier: if they come back within five years, two-thirds of their land shall be restored;

sentences.zh: 十周年內來者，交還一半；

translations.literal: those who come within ten years shall have half returned;
translations.idiomatic: within ten years, half shall be returned;

sentences.zh: 十五周年來者，三分交還一分；

translations.literal: those who come within fifteen years shall have one part in three returned;
translations.idiomatic: within fifteen years, one-third shall be returned;

sentences.zh: 十五周年外來者，不在交還之限。」

translations.literal: those who come after fifteen years are not within the limit of return."
translations.idiomatic: after fifteen years, no land need be returned.”

sentences.zh: 二月戊申，遣使赴西京，賜太子太師致仕侯益、白文珂、宋彥筠等茶藥錢帛各有差，仍降詔存問。

translations.literal: In the second month, on day wushen, envoys were sent to the Western Capital to bestow tea, medicine, money, and silks on the retired Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent Hou Yi, Bai Wenke, Song Yanyun, and others, each in differing amounts, and an edict of inquiry was also issued.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen in the second month envoys were dispatched to the Western Capital with tea, medicine, cash, and silk for the retired Grand Preceptor Hou Yi, Bai Wenke, Song Yanyun, and others in varying amounts, together with an edict of imperial concern.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，詔曰：

translations.literal: On day renxu, an edict stated:
translations.idiomatic: On renxu an edict proclaimed:

sentences.zh: 善操理者不能有全功，善處身者不能無過失。

translations.literal: One who is skilled in governance cannot achieve complete success; one who is skilled in self-conduct cannot be without faults.
translations.idiomatic: Even the ablest administrator cannot achieve perfection, and even the most prudent man cannot avoid error.

sentences.zh: 雖堯、舜、禹、湯之上聖，文、武、成康之至明，尚猶思逆耳之言，求苦口之藥，何況後人之不逮哉！

translations.literal: Although Yao, Shun, Yu, and Tang were supreme sages, and Wen, Wu, Cheng, and Kang were supremely enlightened, they still sought words that grated on the ear and medicine bitter to the mouth—how much more must those who come after and do not reach them!
translations.idiomatic: Yao, Shun, Yu, and Tang were supreme sages; Wen, Wu, Cheng, and Kang were supremely enlightened—yet they still welcomed unwelcome counsel and sought bitter medicine for the state. How much more must lesser rulers do so!

sentences.zh: 朕承先帝之靈，居至尊之位，涉道猶淺，經事未深，常懼昏蒙，不克負荷。

translations.literal: We have received the spirit of the late Emperor and occupy the supreme position; our acquaintance with the Way is still shallow, our experience in affairs not yet deep, and we constantly fear dullness and obscurity, unable to bear the burden.
translations.idiomatic: Having inherited the late Emperor’s mandate and taken the throne, I am still shallow in the Way and inexperienced in governance, and I constantly fear that my dullness will leave me unequal to the burden.

sentences.zh: 自臨宸極，已過周星，至於刑政取舍之間，國家措置之事，豈能盡是，須有未周，朕猶自知，人豈不察。

translations.literal: Since We took the imperial seat, a full year has passed; as to choices in punishments and government and measures for the state, how could all be correct? There must be points not fully covered—We ourselves still know this; would people not perceive it?
translations.idiomatic: Since I ascended the throne more than a year has passed; in criminal law, policy, and state measures, not everything can be right—there are bound to be gaps. I know this myself; surely others see it too.

sentences.zh: 而在位者未有一人指朕躬之過失，食祿者曾無一言論時政之是非，豈朕之寡昧不足與言邪？

translations.literal: Yet among those in office not one has pointed out faults in Our person; among salary recipients not one word on whether current policy is right or wrong—Is it that Our scant understanding is unworthy of speech?
translations.idiomatic: Yet not one official in office has pointed out my personal faults, and not one salaried officer has spoken on whether current policy is right or wrong. Is my ignorance so complete that I am not worth addressing?

sentences.zh: 豈人之循默未肯盡心邪？

translations.literal: Is it that people follow silence and are unwilling to give their full hearts?
translations.idiomatic: Or are men merely following custom and holding back their full loyalty?

sentences.zh: 豈左右前後有所畏忌邪？

translations.literal: Is it that those at Our left and right, before and behind, have some fear and restraint?
translations.idiomatic: Or do those around me harbor fears that keep them silent?

sentences.zh: 豈高卑疏近自生間別邪？

translations.literal: Is it that high and low, distant and near, of themselves create separation and distinction?
translations.idiomatic: Or do rank and distance themselves create barriers between us?

sentences.zh: 古人云：「君子大言受大祿，小言受小祿。

translations.literal: The ancients said: "The gentleman who speaks great words receives great emolument; he who speaks small words receives small emolument."
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said: “A gentleman who offers weighty counsel receives great emolument; one who offers little receives little.”

sentences.zh: 」又云：「官箴王闕。

translations.literal: " They also said: "Officials admonish the king's shortcomings."
translations.idiomatic: ” They also said: “Officials exist to admonish the throne.”

sentences.zh: 」則是士大夫之有祿位，無不言之人。

translations.literal: " Thus among scholar-officials who hold salary and rank, there should be none who do not speak.
translations.idiomatic: ” Thus every salaried scholar-official ought to speak out.

sentences.zh: 然則為人上者，不能感其心而致其言，此朕之過也。

translations.literal: If then one above cannot move their hearts and draw forth their words, this is Our fault.
translations.idiomatic: If I as sovereign have failed to move their hearts and draw forth their counsel, the fault is mine.

sentences.zh: 得不求骨鯁之辭，詢正直之議，共申裨益，庶洽治平。

translations.literal: Must We not seek words like bone in the throat, inquire into upright counsel, together declare what is beneficial, and thereby hope to attain good governance and peace?
translations.idiomatic: I must therefore seek blunt counsel and honest debate, so that together we may improve governance and bring the realm to peace.

sentences.zh: 朕於卿大夫才不能盡知，面不能盡識，若不采其言而觀其行，審其意而察其忠，則何以見器量之深淺，知任用之當否？

translations.literal: We cannot fully know the talents of you ministers and grandees, nor fully recognize your faces; if We do not take their words and observe their conduct, examine their intent and inspect their loyalty, how can We see the depth or shallowness of capacity and know whether appointment is fitting?
translations.idiomatic: I cannot know every minister’s talent or recognize every face; unless I heed your words, watch your conduct, weigh your intent, and test your loyalty, how can I judge your capacity or know whom to appoint?

sentences.zh: 若言之不入，罪實在予；

translations.literal: If words do not enter, the fault is truly in Us;
translations.idiomatic: If your words do not reach me, the fault is truly mine;

sentences.zh: 茍求之不言，咎將誰執！

translations.literal: if We seek counsel and none speaks, upon whom will the blame fall!
translations.idiomatic: but if I ask and you remain silent, upon whom will the blame fall?

sentences.zh: 應內外文武臣僚，今後或有所見所聞，並許上章論諫。

translations.literal: All civil and military officials within and without, hereafter if they have anything seen or heard, are all permitted to submit memorials to discuss and remonstrate.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth all civil and military officials, at court or in the provinces, may memorialize on anything they see or hear.

sentences.zh: 若朕躬之有闕失，得以盡言；

translations.literal: If there are faults in Our person, they may speak fully;
translations.idiomatic: Speak fully of any fault in my person;

sentences.zh: 時政之有瑕疵，勿宜有隱。

translations.literal: if there are flaws in current policy, they should not be concealed.
translations.idiomatic: and do not conceal flaws in current policy.

sentences.zh: 方求名實，豈尚虛華，茍或素不工文，但可直書其事。

translations.literal: We seek substance and reality—how could We esteem empty show? If one is by nature unskilled in writing, he need only write the matter plainly.
translations.idiomatic: I seek substance, not ornament; if you are no stylist, write plainly of the facts.

sentences.zh: 辭有謬誤者，固當舍短，言涉傷忤者，必與留中，所冀盡情，免至多慮。

translations.literal: If the wording has errors, We shall of course overlook the faults; if the words touch on offense, We shall certainly retain them within, hoping that all may speak freely and be spared excessive anxiety.
translations.idiomatic: Errors in wording I will overlook; words that offend I will keep confidential. Speak freely, without undue fear.

sentences.zh: 諸有司局公事者，各宜舉職，事有不便者，革之可也，理有可行者，舉之可也，勿務因循，漸成訛謬。

translations.literal: All offices and bureaus with public duties should each perform their functions; where affairs are inconvenient, they may be reformed; where principle permits action, it may be proposed—do not cling to routine and gradually create error.
translations.idiomatic: Every office should perform its duty: reform what is harmful, propose what is sound, and do not cling to routine until error accumulates.

sentences.zh: 臣僚有出使在外回者，茍或知黎庶之利病，聞官吏之優劣，當具敷奏，以廣聽聞。

translations.literal: Officials who return from missions abroad, if they know the benefits and harms affecting the common people or hear of the excellence or defects of officials, should fully memorialize so as to broaden what is heard.
translations.idiomatic: Officials returning from missions abroad should fully report what they know of the people’s welfare and of officials’ merit or failings, so that my hearing may be broadened.

sentences.zh: 班行職位之中，遷除改轉之際，即當考陳力之輕重，較言事之否臧，奉公切直者當議甄升，臨事蓄縮者須期抑退。

translations.literal: Among the ranks in office, at the time of promotion, removal, or transfer, one should examine the weight of their exertion of strength and compare whether their words on affairs are right or wrong; those devoted to public duty and forthright should be considered for advancement, those who shrink before affairs should be expected to be demoted.
translations.idiomatic: At promotions and transfers, weigh each man’s service and the soundness of his counsel: advance the dutiful and forthright, demote the timid in crisis.

sentences.zh: 翰林學士、兩省官職居侍從，乃論思諫諍之司；

translations.literal: Hanlin academicians and officials of the Two Departments who attend in close service are the offices for deliberation, reflection, remonstrance, and admonition;
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin academicians and Two-Department officials in close attendance are charged with deliberation and remonstrance;

sentences.zh: 御史臺官任處憲綱，是擊搏糾彈之地。

translations.literal: Censorate officials bear the constitutional net; it is the place for striking, seizing, and impeachment.
translations.idiomatic: Censorate officials uphold the law; theirs is the duty of investigation and impeachment.

sentences.zh: 論其職分，尤異群臣，如逐任官內，所獻替啟發彈舉者，至月限滿合遷轉時，宜令中書門下先奏取進止。

translations.literal: In their duties they differ especially from the multitude of officials; for each term in office, the proposals for replacement, enlightenment, and impeachment they submit—when the monthly term is full and transfer is due, the Secretariat and Chancellery should first memorialize and obtain approval.
translations.idiomatic: Their duties set them apart: at each term’s end, when promotion is due, the Secretariat and Chancellery shall first report their memorials and impeachments and obtain imperial approval.

sentences.zh: 三月辛未，以李晏口為靜安軍，其軍南距冀州百里，北距深州三十里，夾胡盧河為壘。

translations.literal: In the third month, on day xinwei, Liyankou was made Jing'an Army; the army was one hundred li south of Jizhou and thirty li north of Shenzhou, with fortresses straddling the Hulu River.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei in the third month Liyankou was established as Jing'an Army, one hundred li south of Jizhou and thirty li north of Shenzhou, with fortifications along the Hulu River.

sentences.zh: （《通鑒》：浚胡盧河在正月，至三月始建軍額。）〉

translations.literal: (Zizhi Tongjian: The dredging of the Hulu River was in the first month; only in the third month was the army designation established.))
translations.idiomatic: (Zizhi Tongjian notes: the Hulu was dredged in the first month, but the army designation was not created until the third month.))

sentences.zh: 先是，貝、冀之境密邇戎疆，居常敵騎涉河而南，馳突往來洞無阻礙，北鄙之地民不安居。

translations.literal: Previously, the border of Bei and Ji closely adjoined the barbarian frontier; enemy cavalry commonly crossed the river southward and rode in sudden raids back and forth with no obstruction, and the people of the northern marches could not live in peace.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Bei–Ji border lay hard against the frontier; enemy horsemen routinely crossed the river to raid at will, and northern villagers could not live in peace.

sentences.zh: 帝乃按圖定策，遣許州節度使王彥超、曹州節度使韓通等領兵他徙，築壘於李晏口，以兵戍守，功未畢，契丹眾尋至，彥超等擊退之。

translations.literal: The Emperor then consulted maps and fixed strategy, sending Wang Yanchao, military governor of Xuzhou, Han Tong, military governor of Caozhou, and others to lead troops elsewhere, build fortresses at Liyankou, and garrison them with troops; the work was not yet complete when Khitan forces soon arrived, and Yanchao and the others drove them back.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor studied the maps and sent Xuzhou commissioner Wang Yanchao, Caozhou commissioner Han Tong, and others to relocate troops and build fortresses at Liyankou. Before the work was finished Khitan forces arrived; Yanchao and his colleagues repulsed them.

sentences.zh: 及壘成，頗扼要害，自是敵騎雖至，不敢涉河，邊民稍得耕牧焉。

translations.literal: When the fortresses were completed, they largely controlled the strategic points; from then on, though enemy cavalry came, they did not dare cross the river, and border people gradually were able to farm and herd.
translations.idiomatic: When the fortresses were finished they commanded the key points; thereafter enemy horsemen dared not cross the river, and border folk could gradually farm and herd again.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，尚書禮部貢院進新及第進士李覃等一十六人所試詩賦、文論、策文等。

translations.literal: On day renchen, the Examination Hall of the Ministry of Rites of the Secretariat presented the poetry, fu, literary essays, and policy essays submitted by the sixteen newly passed jinshi including Li Tan.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen the Ministry of Rites examination hall presented the poetry, fu, essays, and policy papers of the sixteen newly passed jinshi led by Li Tan.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「國家設貢舉之司，求英俊之士，務詢文行，方中科名。

translations.literal: An edict stated: "The state has established the office of tribute examinations to seek outstanding men; it inquires into literary accomplishment and conduct, and only then grants the degree name."
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: “The state holds examinations to seek outstanding men and weighs both learning and conduct before granting the degree.”

sentences.zh: 比聞近年以來，多有濫進，或以年勞而得第，或因媒勢以出身。

translations.literal: We have lately heard that in recent years there have been many who advanced improperly, some gaining the degree through years of service, others entering office through patronage and influence.
translations.idiomatic: Lately we have heard that many have passed improperly—some through seniority alone, others through patronage.

sentences.zh: 今歲所放舉人，試令看驗，果見紕繆，須至去留。

translations.literal: The candidates passed this year were tested and examined; flaws were indeed found, and retention or removal was necessary.
translations.idiomatic: This year’s candidates were re-examined; flaws were found, and some must be kept while others are removed.

sentences.zh: 其李覃、何嚴、楊徽之、趙鄰幾等四人，宜放及第。

translations.literal: Li Tan, He Yan, Yang Huizhi, Zhao Linji, and three others—four men in all—should be granted passage of the degree.
translations.idiomatic: Li Tan, He Yan, Yang Huizhi, and Zhao Linji—the four of them—shall be confirmed as jinshi.

sentences.zh: 其嚴說、武允成、王汾、閭邱舜卿、任惟吉、周度、張慎徽、王翥、馬文、劉選、程浩然、李震等一十二人，藝學未精，並宜勾落，且令苦學，以俟再來。

translations.literal: Yan Shuo, Wu Yuncheng, Wang Fen, Lüqiu Shunqing, Ren Weiji, Zhou Du, Zhang Shenhui, Wang Zhu, Ma Wen, Liu Xuan, Cheng Haoran, Li Zhen, and nine others—twelve men in all—their arts and learning not refined, should all be struck from the list and ordered to study hard, awaiting their return.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shuo, Wu Yuncheng, Wang Fen, Lüqiu Shunqing, Ren Weiji, Zhou Du, Zhang Shenhui, Wang Zhu, Ma Wen, Liu Xuan, Cheng Haoran, and Li Zhen—the twelve of them—lack sufficient mastery; all shall be struck from the rolls and told to study hard and try again.

sentences.zh: 禮部侍郎劉溫叟失於選士，頗屬因循，據其過尤，合行譴謫，尚視寬恕，特與矜容，劉溫叟放罪，其將來貢舉公事，仍令所司別具條理以聞。」

translations.literal: Liu Wensou, Vice Minister of Rites, failed in selecting scholars and was quite negligent; according to his faults he should be censured and demoted, but in view of leniency We specially grant indulgence: Liu Wensou is released from punishment; as to future examination affairs, the responsible offices are still ordered to draw up separate regulations and report."
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Rites Liu Wensou failed in selecting candidates and was unduly lax; by rights he should be punished, but I show leniency and release him from blame. Future examination rules shall be drawn up separately and reported.”

sentences.zh: 夏四月庚戌，以內客省使李彥頵為延州留後。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on day gengxu, Li Yanbin, commissioner of the Inner Reception Bureau, was made acting commissioner of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu in the fourth month of summer, inner reception commissioner Li Yanbin was appointed acting Yanzhou commissioner.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，詔：「應自外新除御史，未經朝謝，行過州府，不得受館驛供給及所在公禮。

translations.literal: On day xinhai, an edict: "Newly appointed censors from outside who have not yet attended court thanksgiving, when passing through prefectures and districts on their journey, must not receive post-station supplies or local official gifts."
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai an edict ordered: “Newly appointed censors from the provinces who have not yet attended court may not accept post-station provisions or local official gifts while traveling through prefectures.”

sentences.zh: 」乙卯，詔於京城四面別築羅城，期以來春興役。

translations.literal: " On day yimao, an edict ordered construction of outer walls on all four sides of the capital, with labor to begin the coming spring.
translations.idiomatic: ” On yimao an edict ordered outer walls built on all four sides of the capital, with work to begin the following spring.

sentences.zh: 戊午，以翰林學士、給事中竇儀為禮部侍郎，依前充職；

translations.literal: On day wuwu, Dou Yi, Hanlin academician and Supervising Secretary, was made Vice Minister of Rites, continuing in his former concurrent duties;
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu Hanlin academician and supervising secretary Dou Yi was named Vice Minister of Rites while retaining his existing posts;

sentences.zh: 以禮部侍郎劉溫叟為太子詹事。

translations.literal: Liu Wensou, Vice Minister of Rites, was made Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: and Liu Wensou (Vice Minister of Rites) became Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，以翰林學士、中書舍人楊昭儉為御史中丞。

translations.literal: On day guihai, Yang Zhaojian, Hanlin academician and Secretariat Drafter, was made Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai Hanlin academician and secretariat drafter Yang Zhaojian was appointed Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 是月，詔翰林學士承旨徐臺符已下二十餘人，各撰《為君難為臣不易論》、《平邊策》各一首，帝親覽之。

translations.literal: That month, an edict ordered Xu Taifu, Hanlin academician-in-chief, and more than twenty others below him each to compose one treatise On the Difficulty of Being Ruler and the Difficulty of Being Minister and one Border-Pacification Stratagem; the Emperor personally reviewed them.
translations.idiomatic: That month the Emperor ordered Hanlin chief Xu Taifu and more than twenty colleagues each to write an essay On the Difficulty of Being Ruler and Minister and a Border-Pacification Stratagem, which he read personally.

sentences.zh: （《宋史·陶蒨傳》：世宗謂宰相曰：「朕觀歷代君臣治平之道，誠為不易，又念唐、晉失德之後，亂臣黠將，僭竊者多。

translations.literal: (Song Shi, Biography of Tao Qian: The Emperor Shizong said to the chief ministers: "We observe the way of rulers and ministers through the ages in achieving order and peace—it is truly not easy; We also recall that after Tang and Jin lost virtue, rebellious ministers and cunning generals who usurped were many."
translations.idiomatic: (Song Shi, biography of Tao Qian: Shizong told his chief ministers: “I see how hard it is for ruler and minister together to bring order; and after Tang and Jin lost their virtue, rebellious ministers and cunning generals usurped power in great numbers.”

sentences.zh: 今中原甫定，吳、蜀、幽、并尚未平附，聲教未能遠被，宣令近臣各為論策，宜導經濟之略。

translations.literal: Now the Central Plain has just been settled, but Wu, Shu, You, and Bing are not yet pacified and attached; civilizing instruction cannot yet reach far. We proclaim that close ministers each compose discourses and stratagems, guiding toward policies of statecraft."
translations.idiomatic: The Central Plain is only now settled; Wu, Shu, You, and Bing are not yet subdued, and imperial influence does not yet reach far. I order my close advisers each to submit policy essays pointing toward practical statecraft.”

sentences.zh: 」乃命承旨徐臺符已下二十餘人，各撰《為君難為臣不易論》、《平邊策》以進。

translations.literal: " He then ordered Xu Taifu, academician-in-chief, and more than twenty others below him each to compose On the Difficulty of Being Ruler and the Difficulty of Being Minister and Border-Pacification Stratagem and present them.
translations.idiomatic: ” He then ordered chief academician Xu Taifu and more than twenty others each to submit the two essays named above.

sentences.zh: 其略率以修文德、來遠人為意，惟蒨與竇儀、楊昭儉、王樸以封疆密邇江、淮，當用師取之。

translations.literal: Their summaries mostly took cultivating civil virtue and drawing distant peoples as their intent; only Qian, with Dou Yi, Yang Zhaojian, and Wang Pu, held that since the frontier closely adjoined the Yangzi and Huai, troops should be used to take it.
translations.idiomatic: Most argued for civil virtue and winning distant peoples; only Tao Qian, with Dou Yi, Yang Zhaojian, and Wang Pu, urged military action because the frontier lay close to the Yangzi and Huai.

sentences.zh: 世宗自克高平，常訓兵講武，思混一天下，及覽其策，欣然聽納，由是平南之意益堅矣。）〉

translations.literal: Shizong, since conquering Gaoping, had constantly trained troops and reviewed arms, thinking to unify all under Heaven; when he read their stratagems he gladly accepted them, and from this his intent to pacify the south grew firmer.))
translations.idiomatic: Since his victory at Gaoping, Shizong had trained troops and dreamed of unifying the realm; reading these essays he gladly accepted them, and his resolve to conquer the south grew firmer still.))

sentences.zh: 五月辛未，回鶻遣使貢方物。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on day xinwei, the Uyghurs sent envoys presenting local products.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei in the fifth month Uyghur envoys presented tribute goods.

sentences.zh: 鳳翔節度使王景上言：「奉詔攻收秦、鳳二州，已於今月一日領軍由大散關路進軍次。

translations.literal: Wang Jing, military governor of Fengxiang, memorialized: "In obedience to an edict to attack and recover Qin and Feng prefectures, on the first of this month I have led the army by the Dasanguan route and am advancing."
translations.idiomatic: Fengxiang commissioner Wang Jing reported: “By imperial order to recover Qin and Feng, on the first of this month I led the army through Dasanguan pass and am advancing.”

sentences.zh: 」先是，晉末契丹入晉，秦州節度使何建以秦、成、階三州入蜀，蜀人又取鳳州。

translations.literal: " Previously, at the end of Jin the Khitan entered Jin; He Jian, military governor of Qinzhou, surrendered Qin, Cheng, and Jie prefectures to Shu, and the Shu people also took Fengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: ” Earlier, at the end of Later Jin the Khitan invaded; Qinzhou commissioner He Jian surrendered Qin, Cheng, and Jie to Shu, and Shu also seized Fengzhou.

sentences.zh: 至是，秦、鳳人戶怨蜀之苛政，相次詣闕，乞舉兵收復舊地，乃詔景與宣徽南院使向訓率師赴焉。

translations.literal: At this time the households of Qin and Feng resented Shu’s harsh government and came one after another to court, begging that troops be raised to recover their old territory; an edict then ordered Jing and Xiang Xun, commissioner of the Southern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat, to lead armies there.
translations.idiomatic: Now the people of Qin and Feng, resenting Shu’s harsh rule, came in succession to court begging for troops to recover their lands; the Emperor ordered Wang Jing and Southern Palace Secretariat commissioner Xiang Xun to lead armies there.

sentences.zh: （《東都事略·王溥傳》：世宗將討秦、鳳，溥薦向拱，遂平之。

translations.literal: (Dongdu Shilüe, Biography of Wang Pu: When Shizong was about to campaign against Qin and Feng, Pu recommended Xiang Gong, and they were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: (Dongdu Shilüe, biography of Wang Pu: When Shizong prepared to attack Qin and Feng, Pu recommended Xiang Gong, and the region was pacified.

sentences.zh: 世宗因宴酌卮酒賜之，曰：「成吾邊功，卿擇帥之力也。」）〉

translations.literal: Shizong at a banquet poured a cup of wine and bestowed it on him, saying: "You have accomplished Our frontier achievement—the power is in your choosing the commander."))
translations.idiomatic: At a banquet Shizong poured him a cup of wine and said: “Our frontier success is owed to your choice of commander.”))

sentences.zh: 甲戌，詔曰：

translations.literal: On day jiaxu, an edict stated:
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu an edict proclaimed:

sentences.zh: 釋氏貞宗，聖人妙道，助世勸善，其利甚優。

translations.literal: The true teaching of the Buddha-Shakya clan is the wondrous Way of the sage; it aids the age and encourages goodness, and its benefit is very great.
translations.idiomatic: Buddhism is the sage’s subtle Way: it aids the age and encourages goodness, and its benefit is profound.

sentences.zh: 前代以來，累有條貫，近年已降，頗紊規繩。

translations.literal: From former ages there have been successive regulations; in recent years downward, rules and cords have been quite disordered.
translations.idiomatic: Former dynasties laid down regulations, but in recent years discipline has fallen into disorder.

sentences.zh: 近覽諸州奏聞，繼有緇徒犯法，蓋無科禁，遂至尤違，私度僧尼，日增猥雜，創修寺院，漸至繁多，鄉村之中其弊轉甚。

translations.literal: Lately reviewing memorials from the prefectures, monks and nuns violating the law have followed one after another; largely because there were no statutory prohibitions, they reached extreme violation—private ordination of monks and nuns daily increased in vulgar profusion, newly built monasteries gradually became numerous, and in villages and countryside the harm grew worse.
translations.idiomatic: Reading recent reports from the prefectures, I find monks and nuns breaking the law in succession—because prohibitions were lacking, abuses have grown extreme: illicit ordinations multiply daily, new monasteries spring up everywhere, and the harm is worst in the countryside.

sentences.zh: 漏網背軍之輩，茍剃削以逃刑；

translations.literal: Those who slipped the net as deserters from the army, if they shaved their heads, escaped punishment;
translations.idiomatic: Deserters who had evaded capture shaved their heads to escape punishment;

sentences.zh: 行奸為盜之徒，托住持而隱惡。

translations.literal: those who practiced wickedness and theft relied on abbotships to hide their evil.
translations.idiomatic: and criminals took refuge in monasteries to hide their crimes.

sentences.zh: 將隆教法，須辨否臧，宜舉舊章，用革前弊。

translations.literal: To exalt the teaching of the Law, right and wrong must be distinguished; former statutes should be raised up to reform previous abuses.
translations.idiomatic: To restore the Dharma we must distinguish right from wrong; old regulations shall be enforced to reform these abuses.

sentences.zh: 諸道府州縣鎮村坊，應有敕額寺院，一切仍舊，其無敕額者，並仰停廢，所有功德佛像及僧尼，並騰並於合留寺院內安置。

translations.literal: In all circuits, prefectures, counties, garrisons, villages, and wards: monasteries with imperial patent shall all remain as before; those without patent shall all be ordered abolished; all merit images of Buddha and monks and nuns shall be transferred and placed within monasteries permitted to remain.
translations.idiomatic: In every circuit, prefecture, county, garrison, village, and ward: monasteries with imperial charters shall remain; those without shall be abolished, and their images, monks, and nuns consolidated into permitted monasteries.

sentences.zh: 天下諸縣城郭內，若無敕額寺院，只於合停廢寺院內，選功德屋宇最多者，或寺院僧尼各留一所，若無尼住，只留僧寺院一所。

translations.literal: Within the walls of all counties under Heaven, if there is no monastery with patent, only from among monasteries to be abolished choose the one with the most merit halls, or leave one monastery each for monks and nuns; if no nuns reside there, leave only one monks’ monastery.
translations.idiomatic: Within county seats lacking chartered monasteries, choose from those to be abolished the one with the most merit halls—or retain one monastery each for monks and nuns; where no nuns reside, retain only one monks’ monastery.

sentences.zh: 諸軍鎮坊郭及二百戶已上者，亦依諸縣例指揮。

translations.literal: Military garrisons, ward settlements, and places with two hundred households or more shall likewise follow the county precedent in their orders.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison towns and settlements of two hundred households or more shall follow the same rules as counties.

sentences.zh: 如邊遠州郡無敕額寺院處，於停廢寺院內僧尼各留兩所。

translations.literal: In remote border prefectures where there are no monasteries with patent, from among abolished monasteries leave two each for monks and nuns.
translations.idiomatic: In remote border prefectures without chartered monasteries, retain two each for monks and nuns from among those abolished.

sentences.zh: 今後並不得創造寺院蘭若。

translations.literal: Hereafter none may newly build monasteries or hermitages.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth no new monasteries or hermitages may be built.

sentences.zh: 王公戚裏諸道節刺已下，今後不得奏請創造寺院及請開置戒壇。

translations.literal: Princes, dukes, imperial affines, circuit commissioners, prefects, and all below—hereafter they may not memorialize requesting construction of monasteries or requesting establishment of ordination platforms.
translations.idiomatic: Princes, imperial affines, military commissioners, prefects, and all below may no longer petition to build monasteries or open ordination platforms.

sentences.zh: 男子女子如有誌願出家者，並取父母、祖父母處分，已孤者取同居伯叔兄處分，候聽許方得出家。

translations.literal: Men and women who wish to leave home must all obtain disposition from parents and grandparents; if orphaned, from uncles and elder brothers of the same household; only after permission is heard may they leave home.
translations.idiomatic: Men and women wishing to take vows must obtain consent from parents and grandparents—or, if orphaned, from uncles and elder brothers in the household—and may leave home only after permission is granted.

sentences.zh: 男年十五已上，念得經文一百紙，或讀得經文五百紙，女年十三已上，念得經文七十紙，或讀得經文三百紙者，經本府陳狀乞剃頭，委錄事參軍本判官試驗經文。

translations.literal: Men aged fifteen or above who can recite one hundred sheets of scripture or read five hundred sheets; women aged thirteen or above who can recite seventy sheets or read three hundred sheets—after petitioning the prefecture for tonsure, the recording secretary and military aide of the prefecture shall test the scriptures.
translations.idiomatic: Men fifteen or older must recite one hundred sheets of scripture or read five hundred; women thirteen or older must recite seventy or read three hundred. They shall petition the prefecture for tonsure and be examined by the recording secretary and military aide.

sentences.zh: 其未剃頭間，須留發髻，如有私剃頭者，卻勒還俗，其本師主決重杖勒還俗，仍配役三年。

translations.literal: Before tonsure they must keep their topknots; if anyone tonsures privately, he shall be compelled to return to lay life; his original master shall be sentenced to heavy beating and compelled to return to lay life, and still assigned corvée for three years.
translations.idiomatic: Before formal tonsure they must keep their hair; illicit tonsure shall force return to lay life, and the master shall be beaten, forced back to lay life, and assigned three years’ corvée.

sentences.zh: 兩京、大名府、京兆府、青州各處置戒壇，候受戒時，兩京委祠部差官引試，其大名府等三處，只委本判官錄事參軍引試。

translations.literal: The Two Capitals, Daming prefecture, Jingzhao prefecture, and Qingzhou shall each establish ordination platforms; when receiving precepts, the Two Capitals shall commission the Bureau of Sacrifices to dispatch officials to conduct examinations; at Daming and the other three places, only the prefectural military aide and recording secretary shall conduct examinations.
translations.idiomatic: Ordination platforms shall be established in the Two Capitals, Daming, Jingzhao, and Qingzhou. In the Two Capitals the Bureau of Sacrifices shall examine candidates; at Daming and the other three, the prefectural military aide and recording secretary shall examine them.

sentences.zh: 如有私受戒者，其本人、師主、臨壇三綱、知事僧尼，並同私剃頭例科罪。

translations.literal: If anyone receives precepts privately, the person himself, his master, the three ranks presiding at the platform, and the managing monks and nuns shall all be punished under the precedent for private tonsure.
translations.idiomatic: Illicit ordination shall punish the candidate, his master, the three presiding officers, and the managing monks and nuns under the same rules as illicit tonsure.

sentences.zh: 應合剃頭受戒人等，逐處聞奏，候敕下，委祠部給付憑由，方得剃頭受戒。

translations.literal: Those who should receive tonsure and precepts shall be reported from each place; after awaiting the edict’s issuance, the Bureau of Sacrifices shall issue credentials, and only then may they receive tonsure and precepts.
translations.idiomatic: Qualified candidates shall be reported from each locality; only after imperial approval and credentials from the Bureau of Sacrifices may tonsure and ordination proceed.

sentences.zh: 應男女有父母、祖父母在，別無兒息侍養，不聽出家。

translations.literal: Men and women who have living parents or grandparents and no other sons or daughters to serve them are not permitted to leave home.
translations.idiomatic: Men and women with living parents or grandparents and no other children to support them may not take vows.

sentences.zh: 曾有罪犯，遭官司刑責之人，及棄背父母、逃亡奴婢、奸人細作、惡逆徒黨、山林亡命、未獲賊徒、負罪潛竄人等，並不得出家剃頭。

translations.literal: Those who have committed crimes and suffered official punishment, who abandoned parents, fugitive slaves, traitors and spies, parties of great wickedness, outlaws in mountains and forests, uncaptured bandits, and those who fled while bearing guilt—all may not leave home or receive tonsure.
translations.idiomatic: Former criminals punished by the courts, those who abandoned parents, fugitive slaves, spies, traitors, outlaws, uncaptured bandits, and fugitives from justice may not take vows or receive tonsure.

sentences.zh: 如有寺院輒容受者，其本人及師主、三綱、知事僧尼、鄰房同住僧，並仰收捉禁勘，申奏取裁。

translations.literal: If any monastery rashly accepts them, the person himself, his master, the three ranks, managing monks and nuns, and monks dwelling in neighboring cells shall all be ordered seized, imprisoned, and interrogated, with memorial to obtain decision.
translations.idiomatic: Monasteries that accept such persons shall have the offender, his master, the three officers, managing monks and nuns, and neighboring monks seized, imprisoned, and reported for imperial decision.

sentences.zh: 僧尼俗士，自前多有舍身、燒臂、煉指、釘截手足、帶鈴掛燈、諸般毀壞身體、戲弄道具、符禁左道、妄稱變現還魂坐化、聖水聖燈妖幻之類，皆是聚眾眩惑流俗，今後一切止絕。

translations.literal: Monks, nuns, and laymen—formerly there were many who offered their bodies, burned their arms, refined their fingers, nailed and cut off hands and feet, wore bells and hung lamps, all sorts of mutilating the body, playing with ritual implements, talismanic prohibitions and heterodox ways, falsely claiming transformations, return of souls, seated extinction, holy water, holy lamps, and demonic illusions—all gathering crowds to dazzle and mislead the vulgar; hereafter all are completely stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Monks, nuns, and lay followers have practiced self-mutilation, burning arms, refining fingers, nailing limbs, wearing bells and lamps, heterodox rites, false claims of miracles, holy water, and demonic illusions to dazzle the masses—all such practices are henceforth forbidden.

sentences.zh: 如有此色人，仰所在嚴斷，遞配邊遠，仍勒歸俗，其所犯罪重者，準格律處分。

translations.literal: If there are such persons, the locality is ordered to punish severely, exile in stages to remote borders, and still compel return to lay life; where their crimes are serious, punish according to statutes and regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Such persons shall be severely punished, exiled in stages to remote regions, and forced back to lay life; serious crimes shall be punished under the penal code.

sentences.zh: 每年造僧帳兩本，其一本奏聞，一本申祠部，逐年四月十五日後，勒諸縣取索管界寺院僧尼數目申州，州司攢帳，至五月終已前文帳到京，僧尼籍帳內無名者，並勒還俗。

translations.literal: Each year two registers of monks shall be made; one memorialized to court, one reported to the Bureau of Sacrifices. After the fifteenth day of the fourth month each year, counties are ordered to demand and collect the numbers of monastery monks and nuns within their jurisdiction and report to the prefecture; the prefecture compiles the register; by the end of the fifth month the aforesaid register must reach the capital; those not named in the monk and nun household register shall all be compelled to return to lay life.
translations.idiomatic: Each year two monk registers shall be compiled—one for the throne, one for the Bureau of Sacrifices. After the fifteenth of the fourth month counties shall report monk and nun counts to the prefecture, which shall compile them; by the end of the fifth month registers must reach the capital, and anyone not listed shall be forced back to lay life.

sentences.zh: 其巡禮行腳，出入往來，一切取便。

translations.literal: As to pilgrimage and traveling on foot, coming and going—all is at convenience.
translations.idiomatic: Pilgrimage and itinerant travel may proceed without restriction.

sentences.zh: 是歲，諸道供到帳籍，所存寺院凡二千六百九十四所，廢寺院凡三萬三百三十六，僧尼系籍者六萬一千二百人。

translations.literal: That year, registers supplied from all circuits showed monasteries retained numbering 2,694 in all, monasteries abolished numbering 30,336 in all, and monks and nuns on the registers numbering 61,200 persons.
translations.idiomatic: That year the circuits reported registers showing 2,694 monasteries retained, 30,336 abolished, and 61,200 registered monks and nuns.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，以刑部侍郎邊光範為戶部侍郎，以前御史中丞裴巽為刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: On day wuyin, Bian Guangfan, Vice Minister of Punishments, was made Vice Minister of Revenue; Pei Xun, former Censor-in-Chief, was made Vice Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin Bian Guangfan (Vice Minister of Punishments) became Vice Minister of Revenue, and former Censor-in-Chief Pei Xun became Vice Minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 己卯，刑部員外郎陳渥賜死，坐檢齊州臨邑縣民田失實也。

translations.literal: On day jimao, Chen Wo, Vice Director of the Ministry of Punishments, was granted death; he sat because in inspecting civilian fields in Linyi county, Qizhou, his report was untrue.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao Chen Wo, vice director of the Ministry of Punishments, was sentenced to death for falsifying his report on civilian fields in Linyi county, Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 渥為人清苦，臨事有守，以微累而當極刑，時論惜之。

translations.literal: Wo was a man of pure hardship; in affairs he had integrity, yet for a slight offense he received extreme punishment, and contemporary opinion pitied him.
translations.idiomatic: Wo lived plainly and held firm in office, yet for a minor offense he suffered capital punishment, and public opinion mourned him.

sentences.zh: 戊子，以沙州留後曹元忠為沙州節度使、檢校太尉、同平章事。

translations.literal: On day wuzi, Cao Yuanzhong, acting commissioner of Shazhou, was made military governor of Shazhou, Grand Preceptor by inspection, and Concurrent Councilor of the Hall of Equal Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi acting Shazhou commissioner Cao Yuanzhong was appointed Shazhou military governor, honorary Grand Preceptor, and concurrent chief councilor.

sentences.zh: 丙申，禮部侍郎竇儀奏，請廢童子、明經二科及條貫考試次第，從之。

translations.literal: On day bingshen, Dou Yi, Vice Minister of Rites, memorialized requesting abolition of the Child Prodigy and Clarified Classics examinations and the regulations for examination order; it was approved.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen Vice Minister of Rites Dou Yi asked to abolish the Child Prodigy and Clarified Classics examinations and their examination regulations; the request was approved.

sentences.zh: 六月己酉，以曹州節度使韓通充西南面行營都虞候。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on day jiyou, Han Tong, military governor of Caozhou, was appointed Chief Adjutant of the Southwestern Field Army.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou in the sixth month Caozhou commissioner Han Tong was named chief adjutant of the southwestern field army.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，以亳州防禦使陳思讓為邢州留後。

translations.literal: On day bingchen, Chen Sirang, defense commissioner of Bozhou, was made acting commissioner of Xingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen Bozhou defense commissioner Chen Sirang was appointed acting Xingzhou commissioner.

sentences.zh: 庚申，詔：「兩京及諸道府州，不得奏薦留守判官、兩使判官、少尹、防禦團練軍事判官，如是隨幕已曾任此職者聽奏。

translations.literal: On day gengshen, an edict: "The Two Capitals and all circuit prefectures and districts may not memorialize recommending acting commissioners' aides, commissioners' aides of the two bureaus, vice prefects, or military aides of defense and training commissioners; if they have already held such posts while on staff, memorializing is permitted."
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen an edict ordered: “The Two Capitals and all circuits may not recommend acting commissioners’ aides, bureau aides, vice prefects, or defense and training aides—except those who have already held such posts on a commissioner’s staff.”

sentences.zh: 防禦團練刺史州，各置推官一員。

translations.literal: Defense, training, and prefectural states shall each establish one investigating official.
translations.idiomatic: Each defense, training, and prefectural state shall appoint one investigating official.

sentences.zh: 」辛酉，廢景州為定遠軍。

translations.literal: " On day xinyou, Jingzhou was abolished and made Dingyuan Army.
translations.idiomatic: ” On xinyou Jingzhou was abolished and redesignated Dingyuan Army.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，以前延州節度使袁鳷為滄州節度使，以前邢州節度使田景鹹為鄧州節度使。

translations.literal: On day guihai, Yuan Zhi, former military governor of Yanzhou, was made military governor of Cangzhou; Tian Jingxian, former military governor of Xingzhou, was made military governor of Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai former Yanzhou commissioner Yuan Zhi took Cangzhou, and former Xingzhou commissioner Tian Jingxian took Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 秋七月丁卯朔，以鳳翔節度使王景兼西南面行營都招討使，以宣徽南院使、鎮安軍節度使向訓兼西南面行營都監。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on the dingmao new moon, Wang Jing, military governor of Fengxiang, was made concurrent Overall Commander for Pacification of the Southwestern Field Army; Xiang Xun, commissioner of the Southern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat and military governor of Zhen'an Army, was made concurrent Overall Supervisor of the Southwestern Field Army.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingmao new moon of the seventh month of autumn, Fengxiang commissioner Wang Jing was named overall pacification commander of the southwestern field army, and Southern Palace Secretariat commissioner Xiang Xun (Zhen'an Army) was named overall supervisor.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，太子太傅、魯國公和凝卒。

translations.literal: On day wuchen, He Ning, Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and Duke of Lu, died.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and Duke of Lu He Ning died.

sentences.zh: 八月癸卯，兵部尚書張昭、太常卿田敏等奏，議減祠祭所用犧牲之數，由是圜丘、方澤及太廟即用太牢，餘皆以羊代之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on day guimao, Zhang Zhao, Minister of War, Tian Min, Minister of Imperial Sacrifices, and others memorialized, discussing reduction of the number of sacrificial victims used in state sacrifices; thereby the Circular Mound, Square Pond, and Imperial Ancestral Temple used the great offering directly, and all others were replaced with sheep.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao in the eighth month War Minister Zhang Zhao, Imperial Sacrifices Minister Tian Min, and others proposed reducing sacrificial animals; thereafter the Circular Mound, Square Pond, and Imperial Temple retained the full offering, while all other rites used sheep instead.

sentences.zh: 丁未，中書侍郎、平章事、判三司景範罷判三司，加銀青光祿大夫，依前中書侍郎、平章事，進封開國伯；

translations.literal: On day dingwei, Jing Fan, Vice Director of the Secretariat, Councilor of the Hall of Equal Affairs, and acting director of the Three Offices, was removed from acting director of the Three Offices, given the Grand Master of Splendid Brightness with Silver Seal, continued as before as Vice Director and Councilor, and advanced in enfeoffment to Founding Baron;
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei Jing Fan (secretariat vice director, chief councilor, and acting director of the Three Offices) was relieved of the Three Offices post, promoted to Silver Seal Grand Master of Splendid Brightness, retained his councilor titles, and enfeoffed Founding Baron;

sentences.zh: 以樞密院承旨張美權判三司。

translations.literal: Zhang Mei, academician-in-chief of the Bureau of Military Affairs, was made acting director of the Three Offices.
translations.idiomatic: and Military Affairs chief academician Zhang Mei was named acting director of the Three Offices.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，詔：「今後應有病患老弱馬，並送同州沙苑監、衛州牧馬監，就彼水草，以盡飲龁之性。

translations.literal: On day xinhai, an edict: "Hereafter all horses that are sick, aged, or weak shall be sent to the Shazhou Pasturage of Tongzhou and the Horse Pasturage of Weizhou, where they may have water and grass and fully satisfy their nature of drinking and grazing."
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai an edict ordered: “Henceforth sick, aged, or weak horses shall be sent to the Shazhou and Weizhou pasturages to graze and recover their strength.”

sentences.zh: 」庚子，太子太師致仕趙暉卒。

translations.literal: " On day gengzi, Zhao Hui, retired Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, died.
translations.idiomatic: ” On gengzi retired Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent Zhao Hui died.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，詔曰：「今後諸處祠祭，應有牲牢、香幣、饌料、供具等，仰委本司官吏躬親檢校，務在精至。

translations.literal: On day yichou, an edict stated: "Hereafter at all places of state sacrifice, victims, incense, silks, food offerings, and ritual implements shall be entrusted to the officials of the responsible bureau to inspect in person, striving for utmost refinement."
translations.idiomatic: On yichou an edict declared: “At all state sacrifices hereafter, victims, incense, offerings, and ritual implements shall be personally inspected by the responsible bureau’s officials with utmost care.”

sentences.zh: 行事儀式，依附《禮經》，大祠祭合用樂者，仍須祀前教習。

translations.literal: The rites and ceremonies shall follow the Classic of Rites; for great sacrifices where music is used, practice must still be held before the sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Rites shall follow the Classic of Rites; where music is required at major sacrifices, it must be rehearsed beforehand.

sentences.zh: 凡關祀事，宜令太常博士及監察御史用心點檢，稍或因循，必行朝典。」

translations.literal: For all matters concerning sacrifice, the Erudites of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and the investigating censors should diligently inspect; if there is the slightest negligence, court statutes must be enforced."
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Sacrifices erudites and investigating censors shall diligently inspect all sacrificial matters; any negligence shall be punished under court law.”

sentences.zh: 九月丙寅朔，詔禁天下銅器，始議立監鑄錢。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the bingyin new moon, an edict prohibited bronze vessels throughout the realm and first discussed establishing a bureau to cast coin.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingyin new moon of the ninth month bronze vessels were banned empire-wide and a mint bureau was first proposed.

sentences.zh: 癸未，以太子賓客趙上交為吏部侍郎，以吏部侍郎於德辰、司徒詡並為太子賓客。

translations.literal: On day guiwei, Zhao Shangjiao, Mentor of the Heir Apparent, was made Vice Minister of Personnel; Yu Dechen and Situ Xu, Vice Ministers of Personnel, were both made Mentors of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei Heir Apparent mentor Zhao Shangjiao became Vice Minister of Personnel, while Vice Ministers Yu Dechen and Situ Xu became Heir Apparent mentors.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，詔文武百僚，今後遇天清節，依近臣例各賜衣服。

translations.literal: On day yiyou, an edict ordered that civil and military officials of all ranks, hereafter on encountering the Tianqing Festival, should each be granted clothing according to the precedent for close ministers.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou an edict granted all civil and military officials festival clothing on Tianqing Day, following the precedent for close ministers.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，西南面招討使王景，部送所獲西川軍校姜暉已下三百人至闕。

translations.literal: On day xinmao, Wang Jing, pacification commissioner of the southwest, escorted to court the three hundred captured Western Shu military officers including Jiang Hui and below.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao southwestern pacification commissioner Wang Jing escorted three hundred captured Western Shu officers led by Jiang Hui to court.

sentences.zh: 甲午，潞州部送先擒到河東兵馬監押程支等二百人至闕。

translations.literal: On day jiawu, Luzhou escorted to court the two hundred men previously captured, including Cheng Zhi, military supervisor of Hedong horse and troops.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu Luzhou escorted two hundred previously captured Hedong officers led by military supervisor Cheng Zhi to court.

sentences.zh: 詔所獲西川、河東軍校已下並釋之，各賜錢帛有差。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that all captured Western Shu and Hedong military officers and below be released, each granted money and silks in differing amounts.
translations.idiomatic: An edict released all captured Western Shu and Hedong officers and granted each cash and silk in varying amounts.

sentences.zh: 閏月壬子，西南面招討使王景奏，大破西川賊軍於黃花谷，擒偽命都監王巒、孫韜等一千五百餘人。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, on day renzi, Wang Jing, southwestern pacification commissioner, memorialized that he had greatly defeated Western Shu rebel troops at Huanghua Valley and captured more than 1,500 men including the bogus-appointed overall supervisor Wang Luan and Sun Tao.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi in the intercalary month Wang Jing reported a great victory over Western Shu rebels at Huanghua Valley, capturing over 1,500 men including bogus overall supervisors Wang Luan and Sun Tao.

sentences.zh: （《九國誌·李廷珪傳》：周師攻秦、鳳，以廷珪為北路行營都統，高彥儔、呂彥珂為招討。

translations.literal: (Jiuguo Zhi, Biography of Li Tinggui: When Zhou troops attacked Qin and Feng, Tinggui was made overall commander of the northern route field army, and Gao Yanchou and Lü Yanke were made pacification commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: (Jiuguo Zhi, biography of Li Tinggui: When Zhou attacked Qin and Feng, Tinggui was named northern route commander, with Gao Yanchou and Lü Yanke as pacification commissioners.

sentences.zh: 廷珪遣先鋒指揮使李進以兵據馬嶺，分兵出斜谷，營於白澗，將腹背以攻周師；

translations.literal: Tinggui sent vanguard commander Li Jin with troops to hold Maling, divided troops to exit Xiegu, and encamped at Baijian, intending to attack Zhou troops from front and rear;
translations.idiomatic: Tinggui sent vanguard commander Li Jin to hold Maling, detached troops through Xiegu pass, and encamped at Baijian to attack the Zhou from front and rear;

sentences.zh: 又遣染院使王巒領兵出唐倉，與周師遇，蜀師敗走，王巒死之。

translations.literal: He also sent dye-house commissioner Wang Luan to lead troops out of Tangcang; they met Zhou troops, Shu troops were defeated and fled, and Wang Luan died.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent dye-house commissioner Wang Luan through Tangcang; the Shu army was defeated and Wang Luan was killed.

sentences.zh: 而馬嶺、斜谷之兵聞之皆退奔，高彥儔與諸將謀退守青泥嶺。

translations.literal: When the troops at Maling and Xiegu heard this they all retreated in flight; Gao Yanchou and the generals planned to withdraw and hold Qingni Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this, the troops at Maling and Xiegu fled; Gao Yanchou and his generals planned to withdraw to Qingni Ridge.

sentences.zh: 由是秦、鳳、階、成之地，皆陷於周矣。）〉

translations.literal: Thus the lands of Qin, Feng, Jie, and Cheng all fell to Zhou.))
translations.idiomatic: Thus Qin, Feng, Jie, and Cheng all fell to Zhou.))

sentences.zh: 癸丑，秦州偽命觀察判官趙比以本城降，詔以比為郢州刺史。

translations.literal: On day guichou, Zhao Bi, bogus-appointed investigating aide of Qinzhou, surrendered the city; an edict made Bi prefect of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou bogus Qinzhou investigating aide Zhao Bi surrendered the city and was appointed Yingzhou prefect.

sentences.zh: （《宋史·趙比傳》：高彥儔出師救援，未至，聞軍敗，因潰歸。

translations.literal: (Song Shi, Biography of Zhao Bi: Gao Yanchou marched out to rescue but had not arrived when he heard the army was defeated and therefore fled back in rout.
translations.idiomatic: (Song Shi, biography of Zhao Bi: Gao Yanchou marched to the rescue but, hearing of defeat before he arrived, fled in rout.

sentences.zh: 比閉門不納，召官屬諭之曰：「今中朝兵甲無敵於天下，自用師西征，戰無不勝，蜀中所遣將皆武勇者，卒皆驍健者，然殺戮遁逃之外，幾無孑遺。

translations.literal: Bi closed the gates and would not admit him, summoned the officials and addressed them: "Now the central court's arms are unmatched under Heaven; since troops were sent west on campaign, in battle there has been no defeat; the generals Shu sent were all brave warriors, the soldiers all fierce and strong—yet apart from slaughter and flight, scarcely one survivor remains."
translations.idiomatic: Bi shut the gates against him and told his staff: “The central court’s arms are unmatched; since the western campaign began they have won every battle. Shu sent its bravest generals and fiercest troops—yet scarcely a man survives slaughter and flight.”

sentences.zh: 我輩安忍坐受其禍，去危就安，當在今日。

translations.literal: How can we bear to sit and receive this calamity? Leaving danger for safety should be today."
translations.idiomatic: How can we sit still and suffer this disaster? We must leave danger for safety—today.”

sentences.zh: 」眾皆俯伏聽命，比遂以城歸順。

translations.literal: " All bowed prostrate and obeyed; Bi then surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: ” All bowed and obeyed, and Bi surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 世宗欲命以藩鎮，宰相範質不可，乃授郢州刺史。）〉

translations.literal: Shizong wished to appoint him to a military governorship, but Chief Minister Fan Zhi objected, and he was therefore made prefect of Yingzhou.))
translations.idiomatic: Shizong wished to give him a military governorship, but Chief Minister Fan Zhi objected, and he received only the Yingzhou prefecture.))

sentences.zh: 先是，帝以西師久次，艱於糧運，命今上乘驛赴軍前，以觀攻戰之勢。

translations.literal: Previously, because the western army had long been stationed and grain transport was difficult, the Emperor ordered the heir apparent to ride post-horses to the army front to observe the situation of attack and battle.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, because the western army had camped long and supply was difficult, the Emperor sent the heir apparent by post relay to the front to observe the campaign.

sentences.zh: 及回，具以事勢上奏，帝甚悅，至是果成功焉。

translations.literal: When he returned, he fully memorialized the situation; the Emperor was very pleased, and at this time success was indeed achieved.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he reported fully on the situation; the Emperor was greatly pleased, and success followed as he had foreseen.

sentences.zh: 甲子，秘書少監許遜責授蔡州別駕，坐先假竇氏圖書隱而不還也。

translations.literal: On day jiazi, Xu Xun, Vice Director of the Secretariat Library, was demoted and appointed Vice Prefect of Caizhou, sitting because he had earlier borrowed books from the Dou clan and concealed them without returning them.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi library vice director Xu Xun was demoted to Caizhou vice prefect for failing to return books borrowed from the Dou family.

sentences.zh: 冬十月庚午，召近臣射於苑中，賜金器鞍馬有差。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on day gengwu, close ministers were summoned to shoot in the park, and gold vessels, saddles, and horses were bestowed in differing amounts.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu in the tenth month of winter the Emperor summoned close ministers to archery in the park and granted gold vessels, saddles, and horses in varying amounts.

sentences.zh: 辛未，成州歸順。

translations.literal: On day xinwei, Chengzhou submitted.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei Chengzhou submitted.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，以給事中王敏為工部侍郎。

translations.literal: On day guiyou, Wang Min, Supervising Secretary, was made Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou supervising secretary Wang Min was appointed Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，高麗國遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: On day wuyin, Koryŏ sent envoys to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin Koryŏ sent tribute envoys to court.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，右散騎常侍康澄責授環州別駕，左司郎中史又元責授商州長史，左驍衛大將軍元霸責授均州別駕，右驍衛將軍林延禔責授登州長史。

translations.literal: On day dingchou, Kang Cheng, Regular Attendant of the Right, was demoted to Vice Prefect of Huanzhou; Shi Youyuan, Director of the Left Bureau, was demoted to Senior Recorder of Shangzhou; Yuan Ba, Great General of the Left Brave Guards, was demoted to Vice Prefect of Junzhou; Lin Yanti, General of the Right Brave Guards, was demoted to Senior Recorder of Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou Kang Cheng (right regular attendant) was demoted to Huanzhou vice prefect; Shi Youyuan (left bureau director) to Shangzhou senior recorder; Yuan Ba (left Brave Guards general) to Junzhou vice prefect; and Lin Yanti (right Brave Guards general) to Dengzhou senior recorder.

sentences.zh: 澄等奉使浙中，回日以私便停留，逾時復命，故有是責。

translations.literal: Cheng and the others had been on mission to Zhe, and on returning delayed for private convenience, reporting back beyond the deadline; therefore they received this punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng and his colleagues, returning from a mission to Zhe, had delayed for private reasons and reported late; hence the demotions.

sentences.zh: 右諫議大夫李知損配流沙門島，坐妄貢章疏，斥讟貴近，及求使兩浙故也。

translations.literal: Li Zhisun, Remonstrance Grandee of the Right, was exiled to Liushamen Island, sitting because he had rashly submitted memorials slandering the eminent and near, and because he had sought a mission to the Two Zhes.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance grandee Li Zhisun was exiled to Liushamen Island for rash memorials slandering high officials and seeking a mission to the Two Zhes.

sentences.zh: 己丑，前太常卿邊蔚卒。

translations.literal: On day jichou, Bian Wei, former Minister of Imperial Sacrifices, died.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou former Imperial Sacrifices Minister Bian Wei died.

sentences.zh: 是月始議南征。

translations.literal: That month discussion of the southern campaign first began.
translations.idiomatic: That month plans for the southern campaign were first discussed.

sentences.zh: 十一月乙未朔，以宰臣李穀為淮南道前軍行營都部署，知廬、壽等州行府事；

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the yimao new moon, Chief Minister Li Gu was made Overall Commander of the Vanguard Field Army of Huainan Circuit and given charge of the mobile headquarters affairs of Lu, Shou, and other prefectures;
translations.idiomatic: On the yimao new moon of the eleventh month chief minister Li Gu was named overall commander of the Huainan vanguard field army with charge of the mobile headquarters at Lu, Shou, and neighboring prefectures;

sentences.zh: 以許州節度使王彥超為行營副部署；

translations.literal: Wang Yanchao, military governor of Xuzhou, was made Deputy Overall Commander of the field army;
translations.idiomatic: Xuzhou commissioner Wang Yanchao was named deputy overall commander;

sentences.zh: 命侍衛馬軍都指揮使韓令坤等一十二將，各帶征行之號以從焉。

translations.literal: Han Lingkun, commander of the Palace Cavalry of the Guard, and eleven other generals were ordered, each bearing a campaign title, to follow.
translations.idiomatic: and twelve generals led by Palace Cavalry commander Han Lingkun were ordered to follow, each bearing a campaign title.

sentences.zh: 己亥，諭淮南州縣，詔曰：

translations.literal: On day jihai, Huainan prefectures and counties were addressed; an edict stated:
translations.idiomatic: On jihai an edict was issued to the Huainan prefectures and counties:

sentences.zh: 朕自纘承基構，統御寰瀛，方當恭己臨朝，誕修文德，豈欲興兵動眾，專耀武功！

translations.literal: We have inherited the foundation and rule all within the seas; We ought to be reverent in person at court and broadly cultivate civil virtue—how would We wish to raise troops and move the multitude, displaying military achievement alone!
translations.idiomatic: Having inherited the throne and ruling the realm, I ought to govern with reverence and cultivate civil virtue—how would I wish to raise armies and glory in war alone!

sentences.zh: 顧茲昏亂之邦，須舉吊伐之義。

translations.literal: But regarding this benighted and disorderly state, We must undertake the principle of consoling the afflicted and punishing the guilty.
translations.idiomatic: Yet this benighted realm compels us to console the suffering and punish the guilty.

sentences.zh: 蠢爾淮甸，敢拒大幫，因唐室之陵遲，接黃寇之紛亂，飛揚跋扈，垂六十年，盜據一方，僭稱偽號。

translations.literal: You fools of the Huai region dare resist the great state; taking advantage of the Tang house's decline and linking with the Yellow Bandits' turmoil, you have been arrogant and overbearing for nearly sixty years, stealing and holding one region, usurping a bogus title.
translations.idiomatic: You of the Huai region dare resist the great state; exploiting Tang’s decline and the Yellow Turban turmoil, you have grown arrogant for nearly sixty years, seizing territory and usurping a bogus title.

sentences.zh: 幸數朝之多事，與北境以交通，厚啟兵端，誘為邊患。

translations.literal: Fortunate in the many troubles of successive dynasties, you have communicated with the northern frontier, greatly opened military incidents, and enticed border calamities.
translations.idiomatic: Fortunate in the troubles of successive dynasties, you have dealt with the northern frontier, provoked war, and stirred border troubles.

sentences.zh: 晉、漢之代，寰海未寧，而乃招納叛亡，朋助兇慝，李金全之據安陸，李守貞之叛河中，大起師徒，來為應援，攻侵高密，殺掠吏民，迫奪閩、越之封疆，塗炭湘、潭之士庶。

translations.literal: In the ages of Jin and Han, the realm was not yet tranquil, yet you recruited fugitives and rebels, befriended the vicious and wicked, aided Li Jinquan in holding Anlu and Li Shouzhen in rebelling at Hezhong, greatly raised armies to come as reinforcements, attacked and invaded Gaomi, killed and plundered officials and people, forced away the territories of Min and Yue, and afflicted the gentry and commoners of Xiang and Tan.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jin and Han eras the realm was unsettled, yet you harbored rebels, aided villains, reinforced Li Jinquan at Anlu and Li Shouzhen at Hezhong, raided Gaomi, slaughtered officials and people, seized Min and Yue territory, and ravaged Xiang and Tan.

sentences.zh: 以至我朝啟運，東魯不庭，發兵而應接叛臣，觀釁而憑淩徐部。

translations.literal: Down to Our dynasty's founding, eastern Lu did not attend court; you sent troops to aid rebel ministers and, watching for openings, relied on them to bully Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Since our dynasty arose, eastern Lu has refused court; you sent troops to aid rebels and bullied Xuzhou whenever opportunity offered.

sentences.zh: 沭陽之役，曲直可知，尚示包荒，猶稽問罪。

translations.literal: At the battle of Shuyang, right and wrong were knowable; We still showed forbearance and still delayed calling you to account.
translations.idiomatic: At Shuyang right and wrong were clear; we still showed forbearance and delayed punishment.

sentences.zh: 邇後維揚一境，連歲阻饑，我國家念彼災荒，大許糴易。

translations.literal: Lately in the Weiyang region famine blocked harvests for successive years; Our state, mindful of that disaster, greatly permitted grain purchases.
translations.idiomatic: Lately the Weiyang region has suffered famine year after year; our state, mindful of the disaster, permitted large grain sales.

sentences.zh: 前後擒獲將士，皆遣放還，自來禁戢邊兵，不令侵撓。

translations.literal: Officers and soldiers captured before and after were all sent back; from the first border troops were forbidden and restrained from raiding.
translations.idiomatic: Captured officers and soldiers were always released; our border troops were forbidden to raid.

sentences.zh: 我無所負，彼實多奸，勾誘契丹至今未已，結連並寇與我為讎，罪惡難名，人神共憤。

translations.literal: We have owed nothing; you have been truly full of treachery, enticing the Khitan down to today without cease, linking with Bing bandits as enemies against Us—crimes hard to name, humans and spirits alike enraged.
translations.idiomatic: We have owed you nothing; you have been treacherous, enticing the Khitan without cease and allying with Bing raiders against us—crimes beyond naming, abhorrent to men and spirits alike.

sentences.zh: 今則推輪命將，鳴鼓出師，征浙右之樓船，下朗陵之戈甲，東西合勢，水陸齊攻。

translations.literal: Now We set the war chariot rolling and appoint generals, beat drums and march forth, summon tower ships of the right of Zhe, descend with spears and armor from Langling, combine forces east and west, and attack together by land and water.
translations.idiomatic: Now we appoint generals, beat the drums, and march: tower ships from western Zhe and arms from Langling shall converge east and west, attacking by land and sea together.

sentences.zh: 吳孫皓之計窮，自當歸命；

translations.literal: When Sun Hao of Wu's stratagems were exhausted, he naturally submitted;
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Hao of Wu was at his wits’ end, he submitted;

sentences.zh: 陳叔寶之數盡，何處偷生！

translations.literal: when Chen Shubao's fate was spent, where could he steal life!
translations.idiomatic: when Chen Shubao’s fate was spent, where could he hide!

sentences.zh: 應淮南將士軍人百姓等，久隔朝廷，莫聞聲教，雖從偽俗，應樂華風，必須善擇安危，早圖去就。

translations.literal: All Huainan officers, soldiers, and common people, long cut off from court and hearing no civilizing instruction—though you follow a bogus custom, you should delight in Chinese culture; you must wisely choose safety and danger and early plan departure or staying.
translations.idiomatic: Officers, soldiers, and people of Huainan, long cut off from court though you follow a bogus regime, should welcome Chinese civilization, weigh safety and danger wisely, and decide your course early.

sentences.zh: 如能投戈獻款，舉郡來降，具牛酒以犒師，納圭符而請命，車服玉帛豈吝旌酬，土地山河誠無愛惜。

translations.literal: If you can cast aside weapons and offer allegiance, surrender whole prefectures, provide oxen and wine to reward the army, and present jade tallies to request commands—carriages, robes, jade, and silks, how could We be stingy in reward? Lands, mountains, and rivers We truly do not begrudge.
translations.idiomatic: If you cast down arms and submit whole prefectures, offering oxen and wine to reward our troops and jade tallies to swear allegiance—carriages, robes, jade, and silk we shall not withhold, nor lands and rivers begrudge.

sentences.zh: 刑賞之令，信若丹青，茍或執迷，寧免後悔。

translations.literal: Orders of punishment and reward are trustworthy as black and red ink; if you cling to delusion, how can you escape regret?
translations.idiomatic: Punishment and reward shall be as sure as written law; cling to delusion and you will regret it.

sentences.zh: 王師所至，軍政甚明，不犯秋毫，有如時雨，百姓父老各務安居，剽擄焚燒必令禁止雲。

translations.literal: Where the royal army arrives, military government is very clear, not violating the slightest, like timely rain; common people and elders each strive for peaceful dwelling; plunder, abduction, and burning are strictly forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Where the imperial army goes discipline shall be strict, harming not a hair, gentle as timely rain; the people shall live in peace, and plunder and burning are strictly forbidden.

sentences.zh: 高麗國王王昭加開府儀同三司、檢校太尉，依前使持節元菟州都督、大義軍使，王如故。

translations.literal: Wang Zhao, King of Koryŏ, was given Grand Master of the Office with Equal Ceremony to the Three Excellencies and Grand Preceptor by inspection, continuing as before as commissioner holding the staff of Yuantu Prefecture and commissioner of the Dayi Army; his kingship was as before.
translations.idiomatic: Koryŏ King Wang Zhao was promoted to honorary Grand Preceptor with Grand Master of the Office with Equal Ceremony to the Three Excellencies, retaining his commission as Yuantu prefect and Dayi Army commissioner; his kingship was unchanged.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，以前滄州節度使李暉為邠州節度使。

translations.literal: On day xinhai, Li Hui, former military governor of Cangzhou, was made military governor of Binzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai former Cangzhou commissioner Li Hui was appointed Binzhou commissioner.

sentences.zh: 壬子，潞州奏，破河東賊軍於祁縣。

translations.literal: On day renzi, Luzhou memorialized that Hedong rebel troops were defeated at Qixian.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi Luzhou reported defeating Hedong rebel troops at Qixian.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，西南面行營都部署王景奏，收復鳳州，獲偽命節度使王環。

translations.literal: On day guichou, Wang Jing, overall commander of the southwestern field army, memorialized that Fengzhou was recovered and the bogus-appointed military governor Wang Huan was captured.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou southwestern field army commander Wang Jing reported recovering Fengzhou and capturing bogus commissioner Wang Huan.

sentences.zh: 乙卯。

translations.literal: On day yimao.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao.

sentences.zh: 曲赦秦、鳳、階、成等州管內罪人，自顯德二年十一月已前，凡有罪犯，無問輕重，一切釋放。

translations.literal: A partial amnesty was granted for criminals within the jurisdictions of Qin, Feng, Jie, Cheng, and other prefectures; from before the eleventh month of Xiande 2, all who had committed crimes, regardless of severity, were entirely released.
translations.idiomatic: A partial amnesty was granted for criminals in Qin, Feng, Jie, Cheng, and related prefectures: all offenses before the eleventh month of Xiande 2, whatever their severity, were pardoned.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，前邠州節度使折從阮卒。

translations.literal: On day dingsi, Zhe Congruan, former military governor of Binzhou, died.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi former Binzhou commissioner Zhe Congruan died.

sentences.zh: 己未，邢州奏，河東劉崇死。

translations.literal: On day jiwei, Xingzhou memorialized that Liu Chong of Hedong had died.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei Xingzhou reported that Liu Chong of Hedong had died.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，淮南前軍都部署李穀奏，先鋒都指揮使白延遇破淮賊於來遠鎮。

translations.literal: On day renxu, Li Gu, overall commander of the Huainan vanguard army, memorialized that Bai Yanyu, vanguard commander, had defeated Huai rebels at Laiyuan town.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu Huainan vanguard commander Li Gu reported that vanguard commander Bai Yanyu had defeated Huai rebels at Laiyuan town.

sentences.zh: 十二月丙寅，以左金吾大將軍蓋萬為右監門上將軍。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on day bingyin, Gai Wan, Great General of the Left Golden Crow, was made Senior General of the Right Gate Watch.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin in the twelfth month left Golden Crow general Gai Wan was appointed senior right Gate Watch general.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，淄州奏，前中書侍郎、同平章事景範卒。

translations.literal: On day dingmao, Zizhou memorialized that Jing Fan, former Vice Director of the Secretariat and Concurrent Councilor, had died.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao Zizhou reported that former secretariat vice director and chief councilor Jing Fan had died.

sentences.zh: 庚午，右金吾衛上將軍王守恩卒。

translations.literal: On day gengwu, Wang Shou'en, Senior General of the Right Golden Crow Guard, died.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu right Golden Crow senior general Wang Shou'en died.

sentences.zh: 辛未，安州奏，盜殺防禦使張穎。

translations.literal: On day xinwei, Anzhou memorialized that bandits had killed Zhang Ying, defense commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei Anzhou reported that bandits had killed defense commissioner Zhang Ying.

sentences.zh: 是日，翰林學士承旨徐臺符卒。

translations.literal: That day, Xu Taifu, Hanlin academician-in-chief, died.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Hanlin chief academician Xu Taifu died.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，李穀奏，破淮賊二千人於壽州城下。

translations.literal: On day jiaxu, Li Gu memorialized that two thousand Huai rebels were defeated below the walls of Shouzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu Li Gu reported defeating two thousand Huai rebels below Shouzhou.

sentences.zh: 丙子，以左諫議大夫、權知開封府事王樸為左散騎常侍，充端明殿學士，依前權知開封府事。

translations.literal: On day bingzi, Wang Pu, Remonstrance Grandee of the Left and acting mayor of Kaifeng, was made Regular Attendant of the Left, appointed academician of the Duanming Hall, and continued as before as acting mayor of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi remonstrance grandee and acting Kaifeng mayor Wang Pu was named left regular attendant and Duanming Hall academician while retaining acting charge of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 永興軍奏，節度使劉詞卒。

translations.literal: Yongxing Army memorialized that Liu Ci, military commissioner, had died.
translations.idiomatic: Yongxing Army reported that commissioner Liu Ci had died.

sentences.zh: 己卯，李穀奏，破淮賊千餘人於山口鎮。

translations.literal: On day jimao, Li Gu memorialized that more than a thousand Huai rebels were defeated at Shankou town.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao Li Gu reported defeating over a thousand Huai rebels at Shankou town.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，樞密使鄭仁誨卒。

translations.literal: On day bingxu, Zheng Renhui, Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, died.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu Military Affairs commissioner Zheng Renhui died.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，西南面行營都部署王景，差人部送所獲偽鳳翔節度使王環至闕。

translations.literal: On day xinmao, Wang Jing, overall commander of the southwestern field army, dispatched men to escort the captured bogus Fengxiang military governor Wang Huan to court.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao southwestern field army commander Wang Jing sent men to escort captured bogus Fengxiang commissioner Wang Huan to court.

sentences.zh: 詔釋之，仍賜鞍馬衣服，尋授右驍衛

translations.literal: An edict released him and still bestowed saddle, horse, and clothing; soon he was appointed to the Right Brave Guards
translations.idiomatic: An edict released him, granted saddle, horse, and clothing, and soon appointed him to the Right Brave Guards

sentences.zh: （按：原本闕一字。）〉

translations.literal: (Note: the original text lacks one character.))
translations.idiomatic: (Note: one character is missing in the original text.))

sentences.zh: 大將軍。

translations.literal: Great General.
translations.idiomatic: Great General.

sentences.zh: 是冬，命起居郎陶文舉征殘租於宋州。

translations.literal: That winter, Tao Wenju, Attendant of the Heir Apparent's Chambers, was ordered to collect overdue rent in Songzhou.
translations.idiomatic: That winter attendant Tao Wenju was ordered to collect overdue rent in Songzhou.

sentences.zh: 文舉本酷吏也，宋民被其刑者凡數千，冤號之聲聞於道路，有悼髦之輩，不勝其刑而死者數人，物議以為不允。

translations.literal: Wenju was originally a harsh official; Song common people punished by him numbered several thousand, and cries of injustice were heard on the roads; there were youths in mourning who could not bear his punishments and several died; public opinion held this unjust.
translations.idiomatic: Wenju was a notorious harsh official; thousands in Song suffered under him, and cries of injustice filled the roads. Several youths died under his punishments, and public opinion condemned the methods as unjust.
